kernels.definition: Electrical resistance describes how strongly a material or device opposes current; Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance for ohmic conductors.

definitionAnchor.quote: The current that flows through most substances is directly proportional to the voltage V applied to it

facts.text: For an ohmic device at fixed temperature, current is proportional to voltage.

anchor.quote: current is proportional to the voltage

facts.text: Resistance depends on material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature.

anchor.quote: resistance depends on the geometry and material

kernels.definition: A DC circuit is a conducting path with steady current, sources, and components whose voltages and currents obey conservation rules.

facts.text: Series components share the same current; parallel branches share the same voltage.
Kirchhoff's junction rule expresses charge conservation, and the loop rule expresses energy conservation.

kernels.definition: A magnetic field describes magnetic influence in space and determines magnetic forces on moving charges and currents.

facts.text: Magnetic field lines form closed loops and do not begin or end on isolated magnetic charges.

kernels.definition: Magnetic force on a moving charge depends on charge, velocity, magnetic field, and the angle between velocity and field.

definitionAnchor.quote: force on a moving charge in a magnetic field

facts.text: The magnetic force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field.

anchor.quote: perpendicular to the velocity and magnetic field

facts.text: A charge moving parallel to a magnetic field experiences no magnetic force.

anchor.quote: zero when velocity is parallel to the field

kernels.definition: Faraday's law states that a changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an emf, with direction constrained by Lenz's law.

definitionAnchor.quote: changing magnetic flux induces an emf

facts.text: Induced current direction opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
Changing field strength, area, or orientation can change magnetic flux.

kernels.definition: Inductance measures how a circuit element resists changes in current by inducing emf through changing magnetic flux.

definitionAnchor.quote: self-induced emf opposes the change in current

facts.text: An inductor stores energy in its magnetic field.

anchor.quote: energy stored in the magnetic field

facts.text: A changing current creates a changing magnetic flux that induces back emf.

anchor.quote: Inductance is the property of a device that tells us how effectively it induces an emf in another device

mcItems.q: If the temperature of an ohmic device is held constant, how does the current relate to the voltage?
op: Current is inversely proportional to voltage
Current is directly proportional to voltage
Current is independent of voltage
Current is proportional to the square of the voltage
mcItems.ex: Current is directly proportional to voltage because for an ohmic device at fixed temperature, current is proportional to voltage.

mcItems.q: Which factor influences the opposition to current in a material?
op: The material's chemical composition
The material's length and cross-sectional area
The material's temperature only
The material's voltage
mcItems.ex: The material's length and cross-sectional area influence resistance because resistance depends on material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature.

Kirchhoff's junction rule expresses charge conservation
Kirchhoff's junction rule expresses current conservation
The loop rule expresses charge conservation
mcItems.ex: Kirchhoff's junction rule expresses charge conservation because it applies to the points where multiple paths meet.

mcItems.q: In a DC circuit, what is true regarding components connected in series?
op: Series components share the same current
Parallel branches share the same voltage
Components in series have different currents
Components in series share the same voltage
mcItems.ex: Series components share the same current because the current flows through every part of the conducting path sequentially.

mcItems.q: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between electrical flow and magnetic influence?
op: Currents generate magnetic fields

Magnetic fields are created by moving charges
Electrical flow dictates the shape of magnetic field lines

They form continuous, closed loops
They are only present around moving currents
They are directly proportional to the current magnitude

zero force
a force perpendicular to the field
a force dependent on velocity

keyTerms.df: The push or pull exerted on a moving electrical charge by a magnetic field.
keyTerms.eg: A current-carrying wire placed in a magnetic field experiences a magnetic force that causes it to move.
keyTerms.mi: The magnetic force is only dependent on the magnetic field strength.

mcItems.q: What causes an electromotive force in a circuit?
op: A changing magnetic flux through a circuit
A constant magnetic field strength
A steady current flow
A fixed resistance value
mcItems.ex: A changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an emf.

mcItems.q: How does the induced current behave?
op: It flows in the same direction as the change in magnetic flux
It flows in the direction that opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it
It is determined solely by the circuit's resistance
It is independent of the magnetic field strength
mcItems.ex: Induced current direction opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.

keyTerms.df: The voltage generated in a closed loop due to a time-varying magnetic environment.
keyTerms.eg: When a magnet is rapidly moved near a coil, it creates a voltage that drives a current through the coil.
keyTerms.mi: The induced electromotive force is caused by the material's resistance to current flow.
keyTerms.cx: The induced electromotive force is caused by a changing magnetic flux through a circuit.

mcItems.q: When a current in a coil changes, what physical phenomenon is induced that results in a back electromotive force?
op: A change in the magnetic field strength
A change in the magnetic flux that induces emf
The storage of energy within the magnetic field
The resistance of the circuit to current variation
mcItems.ex: A change in the magnetic flux that induces emf is the correct answer because a changing current creates a changing magnetic flux that induces back emf, contrasting with the misconception that the inductor stores energy in its magnetic field.

keyTerms.df: A circuit component's property that opposes changes in current by inducing electromotive force through magnetic flux variation.
keyTerms.eg: An inductor resists changes in current by inducing emf through changing magnetic flux.
keyTerms.mi: Inductance is the same as the material's resistance to electrical flow.
keyTerms.cx: Inductance is the property of a circuit element that resists changes in current by inducing emf through changing magnetic flux.
